Luxury electric vehicle maker building the Lucid Air sedan and the Gravity SUV, with in-house battery, motor and software technology. It sells directly to affluent consumers through its own studios and also supplies powertrain technology to other carmakers. Headquartered in Newark, California, with a factory in Casa Grande, Arizona and a plant in Saudi Arabia; founded 2007 as Atieva. Listed on Nasdaq (LCID) since 2021 and majority-owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, which funds its heavy losses. Premium consumer brand with growing but still modest awareness, strong on technology and efficiency credentials.

Electric vehicle maker producing the R1T pickup, R1S SUV and the EDV delivery van, with Amazon as the anchor commercial customer. Sells directly to consumers and fleets and earns software and service revenue, including a technology joint venture with Volkswagen Group. Headquartered in Irvine, California, with its main factory in Normal, Illinois and a new plant planned in Georgia; founded 2009. Listed on Nasdaq (RIVN) since its 2021 IPO. Well-known adventure-oriented consumer brand in North America, with a younger outdoor and tech-minded customer base.

Global automaker formed in 2021 by the merger of Fiat Chrysler and PSA Group, owning brands such as Jeep, Ram, Dodge, Chrysler, Fiat, Peugeot, Citroen, Opel, Vauxhall, Alfa Romeo, Maserati and DS. Sells cars and light commercial vehicles to consumers and fleets in more than 130 markets, with roughly 250,000 employees and revenue above 150 billion euros. Legally based in Amsterdam, with major operations in Turin, Paris and Auburn Hills. Listed in Milan, Paris and New York (STLA). Household brands worldwide, very high consumer visibility.

Large Canadian automobile dealership group operating franchised new and used car, truck and collision businesses, plus parts, service and finance and insurance products. Sells to retail consumers across Canada from around 60 dealerships representing brands such as Chevrolet, Ford, Hyundai, Nissan and BMW. Headquartered in Edmonton, Alberta; founded in 1987. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ACQ). Revenue is in the billions of Canadian dollars. Strong local retail presence in Canadian markets but a dealer brand, not a national consumer name.

Online used car retailer where customers browse, finance, trade in and buy vehicles entirely online, with delivery to the home or pickup from branded car vending machines. Earns money from vehicle sales, financing and warranty products, and sells hundreds of thousands of cars a year across the United States. Headquartered in Tempe, Arizona; founded 2012. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CVNA) since 2017. Well-known US consumer brand with heavy advertising and sports sponsorship history, including some pro sports deals.

Electric vehicle company from Los Angeles area, developing premium EVs such as the FF 91 luxury SUV and lower-priced models, and more recently pushing into embodied AI robotics. Crunchbase describes humanoid and quadruped robot development. Based in Gardena, California, with a plant in Hanford, California; founded 2014, listed on Nasdaq (FFIE, now FFAI) after a 2021 SPAC merger. Has delivered very few vehicles, remains loss-making and dependent on financing, with Chinese-linked backers. Small consumer awareness and a financially fragile sponsorship prospect.

One of the largest US automotive retailers, operating roughly 130 franchised dealerships and collision centers in the United States and the United Kingdom, selling new and used vehicles, parts and service, and arranging financing and insurance. Customers are retail car buyers. Headquartered in Houston, Texas; listed on the New York Stock Exchange (GPI), with annual revenue around 18 billion dollars. Franchise brands include Toyota, Ford, BMW and Mercedes-Benz. Local dealership brand names, so low direct consumer recognition of the Group 1 name itself.

Chinese new energy vehicle maker based in Hangzhou, selling compact electric cars such as the T03, C10 and B10 and range-extender models. Stellantis took a stake of about 21 percent in 2023 and formed Leapmotor International, a joint venture that sells the cars outside China from Hoofddorp, the Netherlands, through Stellantis dealers in Europe and other markets. Founded 2015 and listed in Hong Kong (9863). Budget-friendly electric brand with growing consumer visibility in Europe thanks to Stellantis distribution.

Specialty retailer of automotive aftermarket parts, tools, accessories and supplies, selling to do-it-yourself consumers and professional service providers through more than 6,000 stores in the United States, Mexico and Canada. Earns revenue from retail and commercial parts sales. Headquartered in Springfield, Missouri; founded 1957. Listed on Nasdaq (ORLY) with annual sales above 16 billion dollars and tens of thousands of employees. Well-known US consumer brand, an established motorsport sponsor in NASCAR and IndyCar.

Battery materials company producing silicon-based anode material (Titan Silicon) to replace graphite in lithium-ion batteries, aiming to raise energy density in electric vehicles and consumer electronics. Customers are battery makers and carmakers such as Panasonic and Mercedes-Benz, and it operates a large plant in Moses Lake, Washington. Headquartered in Alameda, California; founded 2011 by former Tesla and Apple engineers. Venture-backed with a valuation reported above 3 billion dollars. B2B materials supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

One of the world's largest vehicle manufacturers, owning Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, Skoda, SEAT/Cupra, Bentley, Lamborghini, Scania, MAN and Ducati, with a large finance arm. Sells cars, trucks and buses to consumers and fleets worldwide, with about 9 million vehicles delivered yearly, revenue near 320 billion euros and over 600,000 employees. Headquartered in Wolfsburg, Germany; founded 1937. Listed in Frankfurt (VOW3) with Porsche SE the controlling shareholder. Household brands in every market and a long-standing motorsport and sports sponsor.

Chinese premium electric vehicle maker selling the NIO, ONVO and firefly brands, known for battery-swapping stations and a strong owner community. Customers are consumers, served via NIO House showrooms and direct sales in China and some European markets such as Germany and Norway. Headquartered in Shanghai; founded 2014 by William Li. Listed in New York (NIO), Hong Kong and Singapore. Delivers several hundred thousand vehicles a year and has long been loss-making. Recognised premium Chinese brand, a former Formula E team owner (now Jaguar's partner).

Chinese conglomerate and the world's largest maker of new energy vehicles, selling battery-electric and plug-in hybrid cars under BYD, Denza, Fangchengbao and Yangwang, plus buses, trucks, batteries, electronics components and solar products. Sells to consumers, fleets and transit agencies, with annual vehicle sales above 4 million and revenue well over 100 billion dollars. Headquartered in Shenzhen; founded 1995 by Wang Chuanfu. Listed in Hong Kong (1211) and Shenzhen, with Berkshire Hathaway historically a shareholder. Fast-growing global consumer brand, also a sports sponsor (UEFA Euro 2024).

Power technology manufacturer designing diesel, natural gas, electric and hydrogen engines, powertrains, generators, filtration, emissions and fuel systems. Customers are truck, bus, construction, mining and rail makers and power-generation users in about 190 countries, with revenue around 34 billion dollars and 70,000 employees. Headquartered in Columbus, Indiana; founded 1919. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CMI). B2B brand with strong recognition among truckers and industrial buyers, and a history of motorsport involvement, including Indianapolis 500 sponsorship.

Global automotive technology supplier created in 2022 when Faurecia acquired Hella, offering seating, interiors, clean mobility, lighting, electronics, lifecycle solutions and cockpit systems to carmakers. B2B, with annual sales of about 27 billion euros and roughly 150,000 employees across 40 countries. Headquartered in Nanterre, near Paris. Listed on Euronext Paris (FRVIA), with Stellantis a significant shareholder. Largely invisible to consumers but strong among car manufacturers; Hella and Faurecia brands carried prior motorsport and Le Mans ties.

French luxury group owning Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, Balenciaga, Alexander McQueen, Brioni and Kering Eyewear, plus jewellery houses. Sells fashion, leather goods, jewellery, watches and eyewear to affluent consumers globally through its own boutiques, e-commerce and wholesale, with revenue around 15 to 20 billion euros. Headquartered in Paris; founded 1963 as Pinault, led by the Pinault family. Listed on Euronext Paris (KER), and also owns the Pinault family's stakes in Puma. Highly visible luxury brand portfolio with fashion and sports-adjacent partnerships.

Japanese automaker selling Nissan, Infiniti and Datsun vehicles, including the Leaf electric car, Ariya, Qashqai and the GT-R, with Renault and Mitsubishi in a long-standing alliance. Sells cars to consumers and fleets worldwide, producing several million vehicles a year and employing over 100,000 people. Headquartered in Yokohama; founded 1933. Listed in Tokyo (7201). Has been restructuring after sharp losses in 2024 and 2025. Household global brand, active in motorsport as a Formula E manufacturer, Super GT and a long-time FIFA and sports sponsor.

French automotive supplier producing driver-assistance sensors (lidar, radar, cameras), lighting, thermal systems, powertrain electrification and interior controls. Customers are global carmakers, with about 20 billion euros of revenue and some 100,000 employees across 29 countries; also an aftermarket parts distributor. Headquartered in Paris; founded 1923. Listed on Euronext Paris (FR). Strong industrial brand in the car industry, with limited consumer awareness although it has links to motorsport such as Le Mans and the World Endurance Championship.

XPENG is a Chinese electric vehicle maker selling smart cars such as the G6, G9, P7+ and Mona models, plus developing flying cars through its Aeroht unit and humanoid robots. Sells to consumers in China and export markets in Europe and Asia, and relies on its in-house XNGP driver-assistance software; sells hundreds of thousands of vehicles yearly. Headquartered in Guangzhou; founded 2014. Listed in New York (XPEV) and Hong Kong (9868), with Volkswagen and Alibaba as investors. Tech-forward Chinese consumer brand expanding in Europe.

Electric performance car brand spun out of Volvo Cars, selling the Polestar 2, 3, 4 and 5 to consumers online and through retail spaces in over 25 markets. Headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, with plants in China and South Carolina and a design team in the UK. Controlled by Geely Holding and Volvo Cars, and listed on Nasdaq (PSNY) via a 2022 SPAC merger. It is loss-making and reliant on parent support. Premium design-led brand with growing awareness and prior motorsport and Formula-style marketing.

Connectivity and sensor technology maker supplying connectors, sensors and harnesses to car makers, industrial automation, aerospace, medical, energy and data-center customers. B2B, with revenue around 16 billion dollars and roughly 90,000 employees in about 140 countries. Tax domicile in Switzerland and operational base in Galway, Ireland and Schaffhausen; US operations in Pennsylvania; spun out of Tyco in 2007. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TEL). Component brand with little public awareness, though its sensors are in many vehicles.

Alkegen is a specialty materials company making engineered products such as battery and thermal protection materials, filtration media, fiber insulation and silicon anode materials for EV batteries, industrial and aerospace uses. Customers are automakers, industrial, energy and consumer product companies; Crunchbase notes automotive and industrial focus. Headquartered in Irving, Texas, formed from Unifrax and Lydall, backed by private equity firm Altus Capital Partners. B2B, little consumer brand awareness; limited public detail beyond this.

Indian electric vehicle maker best known for the S1 electric scooter, with motorbikes and its own cell manufacturing under development at its Futurefactory in Tamil Nadu, plus Krutrim connections via the Ola group. Sells directly to consumers online and via showrooms, making it India's largest e-scooter seller by volume. Headquartered in Bengaluru; founded 2017 by Bhavish Aggarwal. Listed on the NSE and BSE (OLAELEC) since its 2024 IPO. Strong consumer brand awareness in India, though recent service complaints and losses have hurt reputation.

Global maker of electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors, sensors and interconnect systems for the automotive, aerospace, data center, mobile device, industrial and military markets. B2B, selling to OEMs and contract manufacturers with revenue above 15 billion dollars and tens of thousands of employees in many countries. Headquartered in Wallingford, Connecticut; founded 1932. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (APH). Component supplier with minimal consumer awareness, though a large and highly profitable industrial group.

Hut 8 is a North American digital infrastructure company that mines bitcoin, operates high-performance computing and AI data centers, and manages power-intensive sites; it merged with US Bitcoin Corp in 2023 and spun in an American Bitcoin business. Customers are cloud and AI users and bitcoin markets. Based in Miami, Florida, with Canadian roots in Toronto. Listed on Nasdaq and Toronto Stock Exchange (HUT). B2B-focused, with little consumer awareness; revenue sensitive to bitcoin prices.

Saudi Electricity Company is the Kingdom's main power utility, covering generation, transmission and distribution of electricity to residential, commercial, industrial and government customers, with over 10 million subscribers. The input tags it as consumer electronics, which is a misclassification. Headquartered in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia; formed in 2000 by merging regional utilities. Listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul, 5110), with the government and Public Investment Fund as major shareholders. Large state-linked utility, known domestically as a regulated monopoly rather than a consumer brand.

Electric vehicle and clean energy company selling the Model S, 3, X, Y and Cybertruck, plus Powerwall and Megapack storage, solar products, the Supercharger network and autonomy software (Full Self-Driving, robotaxi and Optimus robot efforts). Sells directly to consumers and utilities online and via company stores, with roughly 1.6 to 1.8 million vehicles delivered yearly and over 120,000 employees. Headquartered in Austin, Texas; founded 2003, led by Elon Musk. Listed on Nasdaq (TSLA). Globally famous, no traditional advertising or sports sponsorship.

Chinese consumer electronics and internet company producing smartphones, smart home devices, TVs, wearables, and electric cars (SU7 and YU7), run on its HyperOS and IoT platform. Sells to mass-market consumers through online and retail stores in over 100 countries and earns from hardware plus internet services, with revenue above 50 billion dollars. Headquartered in Beijing; founded 2010 by Lei Jun. Listed in Hong Kong (1810). Well-known value brand in Asia, Europe and emerging markets, with substantial marketing budgets and sports sponsorships.

Specialty finance company that buys and services subprime automobile loans originated by franchised and independent car dealers, serving consumers with limited credit histories who need car financing. Earns interest and fees from its loan portfolio funded through securitizations. Headquartered in Irvine, California; founded 1991. Listed on Nasdaq (CPSS). Operates only in the United States and has a portfolio of several billion dollars. B2B-oriented brand with low consumer awareness, a niche lender rather than a mass-market name.

Online local commerce platform connecting consumers with restaurants, grocery and retail stores for delivery and pickup, including DoorDash Dashpass and the Wolt service in Europe after the 2022 acquisition. Earns commissions and fees from merchants, consumers and advertising, and uses a network of independent couriers (Dashers). Headquartered in San Francisco, California; founded 2013. Listed on Nasdaq (DASH), operating in the United States, Canada, Australia, Japan and Europe with revenue around 10 to 12 billion dollars. High-visibility consumer app brand and a major advertiser.

Medical technology company making imaging equipment (MRI, CT, ultrasound, X-ray), patient monitoring, diagnostics, pharmaceutical diagnostics contrast agents and digital health software. Customers are hospitals, clinics and healthcare systems worldwide; revenue around 20 billion dollars and approximately 50,000 employees. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois; spun out of General Electric in January 2023 and listed on Nasdaq (GEHC). B2B healthcare brand with solid recognition among clinicians and little consumer-level visibility.

One of China's largest e-commerce companies, selling electronics, appliances, groceries and general merchandise with its own logistics network, plus JD Health, JD Logistics and JD Industrials. Operates a direct retail model and third-party marketplace, serving hundreds of millions of Chinese consumers and businesses with annual revenue above 150 billion dollars. Headquartered in Beijing; founded 1998 by Richard Liu. Listed on Nasdaq (JD) and in Hong Kong (9618). Very strong consumer brand in China, with limited recognition elsewhere though it is expanding in Europe.

Semiconductor maker producing microcontrollers, analog chips, FPGAs, memory and security devices used in automotive, industrial, aerospace, consumer and data-center applications. B2B, selling through distributors and directly to equipment makers, with revenue around 5 to 8 billion dollars and roughly 20,000 employees. Headquartered in Chandler, Arizona; founded 1989. Listed on Nasdaq (MCHP). The brand is well known to engineers and designers but has little consumer visibility.

Operates Paytm, one of India's best-known mobile payments and financial services platforms, offering UPI payments, wallet, QR code and card-reader devices for merchants, loans, insurance distribution and ticketing. Serves hundreds of millions of consumers and millions of merchants, earning from payments, financial services and marketing. Headquartered in Noida, Uttar Pradesh; founded 2010 by Vijay Shekhar Sharma. Listed on the NSE and BSE (PAYTM) since a 2021 IPO. A regulator action against Paytm Payments Bank in 2024 hit growth. Highly visible consumer brand in India, formerly cricket sponsor.

Semiconductor company making power and sensing chips, including silicon carbide power devices and image sensors, for car electrification, ADAS, industrial automation, energy infrastructure and AI data centers. Customers are carmakers and industrial equipment makers, with revenue of roughly 6 to 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona; formerly ON Semiconductor, with a name change to onsemi in 2021. Listed on Nasdaq (ON). B2B brand with limited public recognition, though it has had motorsport sponsorship links.

Retail investing platform offering commission-free trading of stocks, ETFs, options, cryptocurrency, retirement accounts and a premium subscription (Robinhood Gold), plus a credit card and event contracts. Customers are mostly younger US retail investors, with over 25 million funded accounts. Revenue comes from payment for order flow, interest income, subscriptions and crypto trading. Headquartered in Menlo Park, California; founded 2013. Listed on Nasdaq (HOOD) since 2021 and added to the S&P 500 in 2025. Strong consumer fintech brand with high awareness among US retail investors.

Saudi-based buy now pay later fintech allowing consumers to split purchases into instalments at online and in-store merchants across Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Kuwait, alongside shopping and card products. Earns merchant fees and consumer fees, with millions of users and thousands of partner retailers. Headquartered in Riyadh; founded 2020. Backed by investors such as Sanabil, Checkout.com and Shorooq; became a unicorn after a 2023 debt financing. Well-known consumer brand in the Gulf and an active regional sports and event sponsor.

AI lending marketplace that uses machine learning to assess credit risk, connecting consumers who want personal, auto and home equity loans with partner banks and credit unions. Earns referral and platform fees from lenders, and has originated tens of billions of dollars in loans. Headquartered in San Mateo, California, with an operations hub in Columbus, Ohio; founded 2012. Listed on Nasdaq (UPST). Shares volatile with interest rate cycles. B2B2C model: banks are customers, with modest consumer brand awareness in the United States.

Diversified power management company making electrical products (switchgear, UPS, circuit breakers), hydraulics, aerospace fuel systems and vehicle components, plus data center power systems. Customers are utilities, data centers, industrial companies, aircraft makers and truck and car manufacturers, with revenue around 25 billion dollars and about 90,000 employees in over 160 countries. Headquartered in Dublin, Ireland; operational roots in Cleveland, Ohio, founded 1911. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ETN). B2B brand with modest consumer awareness.

Global automotive technology supplier producing vehicle architecture, active safety and ADAS software, connectors, wiring and displays for car makers; it has been separating its electrical distribution systems business. Customers are global automakers, with revenue around 20 billion dollars and over 100,000 employees. Legally domiciled in Schaffhausen, Switzerland; origins in Delphi Automotive with major operations in Troy, Michigan and Dublin. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (APTV). B2B brand with limited public awareness, though Aptiv has sponsored motorsport, notably as a Jaguar TCS Racing partner in Formula E.

Aurora Innovation develops the Aurora Driver self-driving system for long-haul trucks, and started driverless commercial freight service on Texas highways in 2025. Customers are trucking, freight and logistics firms such as Uber Freight, Hirschbach and Werner, with partners including Volvo and PACCAR. Headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; founded 2017 by Chris Urmson and former Google and Uber staff. Listed on Nasdaq (AUR) since 2021, still loss-making. B2B technology brand with little general public awareness.

Automotive Cells Company (ACC) is a European joint venture of Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz and TotalEnergies' Saft, building lithium-ion battery gigafactories to supply electric cars. Its first plant is in Billy-Berclau Douvrin, northern France, with further sites planned in Germany and Italy, some of which were postponed. Customers are the shareholders and other carmakers; the input shows around 4.4 billion euros in funding. Headquartered in Bruges, near Bordeaux. B2B and privately held, so little consumer awareness.

BAIC BluePark New Energy Technology is the electric vehicle arm of state-owned Beijing Automotive Group, producing the ARCFOX premium electric brand and earlier EU-series cars. Sells to consumers and fleets in China and some export markets, with co-development ties to Huawei in its Stelato-type smart models and Magna. Headquartered in Beijing; listed in Shanghai (600733). State-controlled and loss-making in recent years. Mid-level consumer awareness in China, and a past Formula E sponsor/team partner (ARCFOX Racing).

Hozon New Energy Automobile, better known by its Neta brand, is a Chinese EV maker based in Shanghai selling affordable electric SUVs and hatchbacks (Neta V, Neta U, Neta X) to consumers in China and Southeast Asia. Founded 2014 and backed by Baidu, Tencent-linked investors and local government funds. It raised tens of billions of yuan but ran into severe cash problems in 2024 and entered bankruptcy restructuring in 2025. Once a prominent budget EV brand in China with notable market share growth.

Nikola Corporation developed battery-electric and hydrogen fuel cell heavy-duty trucks (Tre BEV and Tre FCEV) for fleets and ran hydrogen fueling infrastructure. Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, with a factory in Coolidge; founded 2014 and listed on Nasdaq (NKLA) after a 2020 SPAC merger. Founder Trevor Milton was convicted of fraud and later pardoned in 2025; the company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in February 2025 and its assets were sold. Formerly widely known in the US, now defunct.

StarPlus Energy is a joint venture between Stellantis and Samsung SDI that builds electric vehicle battery plants in Kokomo, Indiana, with a second plant planned there. It supplies lithium-ion cells and modules to Stellantis's North American vehicle lines, with investment cited at several billion dollars. Based in Kokomo, Indiana; formed in 2022. Private joint venture with strategic backing from two large industrial groups. B2B manufacturing company with no consumer brand profile, so limited relevance for consumer sponsorship.

T3 Travel (T3 Chuxing) is a Chinese ride-hailing platform backed by FAW, Dongfeng and Changan, offering app-based car rides with company-owned electric vehicles and a focus on safety. Based in Nanjing, Jiangsu; launched around 2019 with funding over 19 billion yuan. Operates in dozens of Chinese cities with millions of daily rides and revenue from fares. Owned by a consortium of state-owned automakers and investors including Tencent, Alibaba and Suning. Known consumer app in China with limited international profile.

Global manufacturer of plastic components and systems for the automotive industry, including air induction and fluid management parts, interior and exterior trim, and fuel systems. Customers are carmakers worldwide, which it supplies from a network of plants across North America, Europe and Asia. Headquartered in Toronto, Ontario; it was acquired by private equity firm Apollo Global Management in 2021 (previously owned by Cerberus and Tinicum) and is privately held. B2B supplier with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

Largest automotive seating supplier in the world, designing and manufacturing seat structures, foam, trim and complete seats for major carmakers including Ford, Toyota, Volkswagen and Stellantis. Revenue is around 14 to 15 billion dollars from plants across more than 30 countries, with some 70,000 employees. Headquartered in Plymouth, Michigan, with Irish tax domicile; spun off from Johnson Controls in 2016. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ADNT). B2B brand with very limited consumer awareness.

Automotive aftermarket parts retailer selling batteries, brakes, filters, oil and accessories to do-it-yourself customers and professional installers through Advance Auto Parts, Carquest and Worldpac stores in the United States and Canada. Operates around 4,000 stores with annual sales of roughly 9 billion dollars. Headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina; founded 1932. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (AAP); restructured in 2024 and 2025 with store closures and the sale of Worldpac. Familiar US retail name with moderate consumer awareness.

Used vehicle retailer and in-house lender in the United States, selling affordable pre-owned cars and financing them to buyers with limited or impaired credit through more than 150 dealerships in mostly smaller Southern and Midwestern communities. Earns money from car sales and interest on its loan portfolio. Headquartered in Rogers, Arkansas; founded 1981. Listed on Nasdaq (CRMT). Regional consumer brand, not widely known nationally.

Europe's largest wholesale and online used car trading platform, with the Autohero brand for retail sales and the wirkaufendeinauto.de service for consumer vehicle purchases. Buys cars from private sellers and dealers and sells to dealers across about 30 countries, selling hundreds of thousands of vehicles annually with revenue near 6 billion euros. Headquartered in Berlin; founded 2012. Listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (AG1) since 2021, with SoftBank a major backer. Autohero is a growing consumer brand; AUTO1 itself is largely B2B.

Leading Chinese online automotive platform providing car pricing, reviews, dealer listings, used car transactions, financing and insurance referrals to millions of users. Revenue comes from dealer subscriptions, advertising by carmakers and transaction services. Headquartered in Beijing; founded 2008. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ATHM) and in Hong Kong (2518), with Ping An Insurance as main shareholder. Very well known among Chinese car shoppers and a strong media channel for automotive advertisers.

Avatr Technology is a Chinese premium electric vehicle brand owned by Changan Automobile with CATL and Huawei as technology and investment partners. Sells the Avatr 11, 12 and 07 models to consumers in China and has begun export. Based in Chongqing; launched 2018 as a Changan Automobile project. Has raised funding at multi-billion dollar valuations and filed for a Hong Kong listing. Rising smart EV brand with growing awareness in China and early international presence.

Maker of recreational vehicles under the Sea-Doo, Ski-Doo, Can-Am off-road and on-road vehicles, Lynx snowmobile and Evinrude outboard brands. Sells to consumers through dealers worldwide with revenue around 8 billion Canadian dollars. Headquartered in Valcourt, Quebec; spun out of Bombardier in 2003 and now owned by the Beaudoin family and Bain Capital along with public shareholders. Listed on the Toronto and Nasdaq exchanges (DOO / BRP). Strong consumer brands and a regular sponsor of motorsport and action sports.

Operator of public direct current fast charging stations for electric vehicles in the United States, with a network of over 4,000 stalls serving drivers, rideshare fleets and automaker partners such as GM and Tesla-compatible customers. Earns from charging sessions, subscriptions, partnerships and incentives. Headquartered in Los Angeles, California; founded 2010. Listed on Nasdaq (EVGO) via a 2021 SPAC deal. Reasonably known to EV drivers, with a US Department of Energy loan guarantee to expand charging.

Geely Holding Group is a privately owned Chinese automotive group founded by Li Shufu in 1986, owning Volvo Cars, Polestar, Lotus, Zeekr, Lynk & Co, Geely Auto, LEVC and Proton stakes, and the Zeekr and Radar EV brands. Sells passenger cars worldwide, with groupwide sales above 3 million vehicles a year. Headquartered in Hangzhou, Zhejiang. Subsidiary Geely Automobile Holdings is listed in Hong Kong. Large global footprint but the Geely name itself is mainly recognised in Asia, Europe and emerging markets.

British premium carmaker producing Jaguar, Land Rover, Range Rover and Defender vehicles, owned by India's Tata Motors since 2008. Sells luxury cars and SUVs globally, around 400,000 vehicles a year and revenue of about 29 billion pounds. Headquartered in Coventry, with plants in Solihull, Halewood and Slovakia and a rebrand toward an electric Jaguar from 2025. Wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Motors. Iconic consumer brands, with sponsorship experience in Formula E, sailing, cycling and the America's Cup.

Canadian global automotive supplier and contract vehicle assembler producing body structures, seating, mirrors, powertrain systems and complete vehicles (Magna Steyr in Graz). Customers are global carmakers, with revenue around 40 billion dollars and about 170,000 employees. Headquartered in Aurora, Ontario; founded 1957 by Frank Stronach. Listed on the New York and Toronto stock exchanges (MGA). B2B, building cars for brands like BMW, Jaguar and Mercedes-Benz, with little consumer brand awareness.

Indian non-bank finance company specialising in loans for used commercial vehicles such as trucks, to small road transport operators, as well as other lending. Now part of Shriram Finance, which merged Shriram Transport Finance and Shriram City Union Finance in late 2022. Headquartered in Mumbai; operates through thousands of branches and holds assets of several lakh crore rupees. Listed on the NSE and BSE (SHRIRAMFIN). Well known in India's trucking and rural lending community, but a niche financial brand.

Boyd Group Services operates a large network of collision repair shops under the Gerber Collision & Glass brand in the United States and Boyd Autobody in Canada, plus Gerber National Claim Services. Customers are drivers and insurance companies who pay for accident repair; over 1,000 locations. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (BYD) with revenue around 3 billion dollars. Gerber Collision is a familiar US repair brand, mostly through insurance referrals.

Global mobility and delivery platform operating Uber ride-hailing, Uber Eats food and grocery delivery, Uber Freight and autonomous vehicle partnerships. Earns commissions from drivers, couriers and merchants plus advertising and subscriptions (Uber One), serving well over 150 million monthly users in more than 70 countries. Headquartered in San Francisco, California; founded 2009. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (UBER) with revenue around 40 to 50 billion dollars. Household consumer brand worldwide and a sports sponsor in football and other leagues.

Social media platform formerly known as Twitter, for short posts, news, video and live conversations, now with Grok AI and X Premium subscriptions, and part of Elon Musk's xAI group after a 2025 merger. Earns from advertising and subscriptions with several hundred million monthly users. Operating base listed in San Francisco, with Bastrop, Texas shown in the input. Acquired by Elon Musk for 44 billion dollars in 2022 and delisted; private. Global mass-market brand, though advertisers have been cautious since the takeover.

407 ETR operates the 407 Express Toll Route, a barrier-free electronic toll highway across the northern Greater Toronto Area in Ontario, charging drivers by distance and time of day via transponders and license plate billing. Revenue is toll income, around 1.5 billion Canadian dollars. Located in Woodbridge, Ontario; opened in 1997 and leased by the Ontario government to a private consortium (Cintra, CDPQ and SNC-Lavalin) until 2098. Well known to Ontario drivers, though not a typical sponsoring brand. The input classes it as software, which is incorrect.

Financial technology company behind Square (payments and software for merchants), Cash App (consumer payments, bitcoin and banking), Afterpay buy now pay later, Tidal music and Bitcoin tools such as Proto. Earns from transaction fees, subscriptions and bitcoin revenue, with revenue around 24 billion dollars. Headquartered in Oakland, California; founded 2009 by Jack Dorsey as Square and renamed Block in 2021. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (XYZ, formerly SQ). Strong consumer and small business brands, with sports and music sponsorship activity.

Software company providing IT asset management, software license optimisation, cloud cost management (FinOps) and software vulnerability tools, used by enterprises to control technology spend. Customers are large enterprises and managed service providers worldwide. Headquartered in Itasca, Illinois; founded 1987. Private equity owned, with Thoma Bravo having bought it in 2020 and Vista Equity Partners among earlier backers. B2B brand known to IT leaders, with little consumer awareness, though it sponsors some events and sporting links.

German semiconductor group making power chips, microcontrollers, sensors and security devices for cars, industrial equipment, renewable energy, data centers and payment cards. B2B sales to carmakers and manufacturers, with revenue of about 15 billion euros and over 58,000 employees. Headquartered in Neubiberg near Munich; spun out of Siemens in 1999. Listed in Frankfurt (IFX) and a DAX member. Market leader in automotive and power semiconductors, relatively low consumer visibility though it has sponsored sport, including football clubs and a Formula E team link.

Saudi-Emirati e-commerce platform launched in 2017 by Mohamed Alabbar, backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, offering electronics, fashion, groceries and home goods through the noon app and noon Minutes, plus Namshi fashion and noon Food. Operates in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, with tens of millions of customers. Headquarters listed in Riyadh, with Dubai a base. Privately held. Leading regional online marketplace with strong consumer awareness across the Gulf and heavy advertising.

Payments processor providing integrated payment processing and software to restaurants, hotels, stadiums, retailers and online businesses, including POS systems and acquired brands such as Finaro and Global Blue. Earns from processing fees and software subscriptions, handling hundreds of billions in payment volume. Headquartered in Center Valley, Pennsylvania (formerly Allentown); founded 1999 by Jared Isaacman. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FOUR). B2B payments brand with small consumer profile, but active in sports venue partnerships and it sponsored motorsport events.

Camera and social messaging company behind Snapchat, with augmented reality Lenses, Spectacles smart glasses and Snapchat+ subscriptions. Earns from advertising and subscriptions with about 450 million daily active users, mainly younger demographics. Headquartered in Santa Monica, California; founded 2011. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (SNAP) with revenue around 5 billion dollars. Mass-market consumer app, widely used by teens and young adults, and has run content partnerships with major sports leagues.

Electronic market maker and liquidity provider trading equities, options, futures, fixed income and crypto across more than 50 countries, also providing execution tools and analytics to institutions. Earns from trading spreads and technology services. Headquartered in New York; founded 2008 by Vincent Viola; Virtu also acquired ITG in 2019. Listed on Nasdaq (VIRT). Institutional brand with limited public awareness, but has a motorsport sponsorship link through the Williams Formula 1 team.

Ather Energy is an Indian electric two-wheeler company producing Ather 450 and Rizta scooters and building its own fast-charging network (Ather Grid) and software. Sells directly to consumers through experience centres across India, with Hero MotoCorp as a major shareholder. Headquartered in Bengaluru; founded 2013. Listed on the NSE and BSE (ATHERENERGY) since a 2025 IPO. Premium e-scooter brand with strong awareness among Indian EV buyers.

Geely Automobile Holdings is the main listed car-making arm of Geely Holding, producing Geely, Lynk & Co and Zeekr vehicles (Zeekr merged back in 2025), selling more than 2 million cars a year, plus exports. Customers are consumers in China and overseas. Headquartered in Hong Kong (Wan Chai) with operations in Hangzhou. Listed in Hong Kong (0175), controlled by Li Shufu. Large Chinese automaker with growing exports and a footprint in Europe via Lynk & Co.

Global adhesives company producing industrial adhesives, sealants and coatings used in packaging, electronics, hygiene products, construction, automotive, and the clean energy sectors. B2B, selling to manufacturers in over 35 countries with revenue near 3.5 billion dollars and about 7,000 employees. Headquartered in Vadnais Heights (St Paul), Minnesota; founded 1887. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FUL). Little consumer awareness, though its hot-melt adhesives are in many everyday products.

Shenzhou Automotive Technology is a Chinese company headquartered in Wuhan, Hubei, focused on developing and selling automotive technologies and vehicles, according to its Crunchbase description. Funding recorded is about 8.2 billion yuan. Crunchbase tags it as automotive and autonomous driving. No further details are available from the input. Limited public information - check before outreach.

Goodyear Tire & Rubber is one of the world's largest tire makers, selling tires under Goodyear, Dunlop, Cooper and Kelly brands for cars, trucks, aircraft and racing, plus retail and auto service centres. Customers are consumers, fleets and carmakers through dealers and owned stores, with sales near 19 billion dollars. Headquartered in Akron, Ohio; founded 1898. Listed on Nasdaq (GT). Iconic consumer brand and a long-time NASCAR, IndyCar and Le Mans partner, with the Goodyear blimp.

Traton is the commercial vehicle holding of Volkswagen Group, owning Scania, MAN, International and Volkswagen Truck & Bus brands. Sells trucks, buses and engines worldwide, with revenue near 47 billion euros and about 100,000 employees, and offers financing and services. Headquartered in Munich; listed in Frankfurt (8TRA) with Volkswagen holding about 90 percent. B2B vehicle brand, widely known to fleets, with limited consumer visibility though Scania and MAN brands carry sports and truck racing associations.

Digital Currency X Technology is a Chinese company based in Jilin that, according to Crunchbase, develops and produces electric vehicle products and is tagged as automotive. No further details are available in the provided data, and the name may be a former or alternate name of another business. Funding listed is about 1.05 billion dollars. Limited public information - check before outreach.

ECARX is a Chinese automotive technology company supplying smart cockpit systems, in-car infotainment, compute platforms and software to carmakers such as Geely, Lynk & Co, Volvo, Polestar and Lotus. Founded 2017 as part of the Geely ecosystem, with research sites in China and Europe. The input lists London as headquarters, while its main operations are in Hubei, Shanghai and Gothenburg. Listed on Nasdaq (ECX) since 2022 via a SPAC merger. B2B supplier with limited public awareness.

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is the joint venture formed by Rivian and Volkswagen Group in 2024 to co-develop software and electrical architecture for electric vehicles. Volkswagen has committed up to 5.8 billion dollars in staged investment and the venture targets Volkswagen's next-generation cars from 2027. Based in Palo Alto, California. Crunchbase notes it develops scalable software-defined vehicle platforms. B2B technology partnership with no consumer brand of its own.

South Korea's dominant search engine and internet platform, offering Naver search, webtoons, shopping, maps, payments (Naver Pay), cloud and AI (HyperCLOVA X) as well as the LINE messaging stake via LY Corp. Earns from advertising, commerce and fintech, with annual revenue about 10 trillion won. Headquartered in Seongnam, Gyeonggi; founded 1999. Listed on the Korea Exchange (035420). Very strong consumer brand in Korea and Japan with Webtoon global reach, and active in cultural and esports sponsorship.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company is the world's largest contract chipmaker, producing advanced processors for Apple, Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and others on leading-edge nodes. Revenue is about 90 to 120 billion dollars with margins among the highest in industry. Headquartered in Hsinchu, Taiwan; founded 1987. Listed in Taipei (2330) and New York (TSM), with a market value above 1 trillion dollars. B2B foundry with limited consumer brand awareness and very little traditional sponsorship activity.

Korean electronics giant making smartphones (Galaxy), TVs, home appliances, memory chips and display panels, sold to consumers and businesses worldwide. Revenue is roughly 200 to 250 billion dollars with about 260,000 employees. Headquartered in Seoul; founded 1969 and the flagship of the Samsung group. Listed on the Korea Exchange (005930). One of the world's most recognised consumer brands, with a long record as a global sponsor of the Olympics, football and other sports.

Vietnamese electric vehicle manufacturer producing the VF 3, VF 5, VF 6, VF 7, VF 8 and VF 9 models, a subsidiary of the conglomerate Vingroup, founded by Pham Nhat Vuong in 2017. Builds in Hai Phong, Vietnam and is constructing a plant in North Carolina and India. Sells cars and e-scooters to consumers in Vietnam, North America, Europe and Asia. Listed on Nasdaq (VFS) since a 2023 SPAC merger, with continuing losses. Strong in Vietnam, still emerging abroad, and has pursued sports sponsorship.

CleanCapital is a New York-based clean energy investment platform that acquires, owns and operates solar, storage and other renewable energy projects, offering an online platform for investors to access commercial and utility scale assets. Founded around 2017 by Ben Hallock and Robert Clingan. Raised several hundred million dollars of equity and debt capital; the input shows about 1.8 billion dollars of total funding. B2B and investor-facing brand with no consumer visibility.

Kraken is a US cryptocurrency exchange offering trading, staking, margin, futures and custody services to retail and institutional customers in many countries, plus Kraken Pro, NFT and a Kraken Wallet. Founded 2011 by Jesse Powell. Earns trading fees and other revenue; has raised funding at a valuation around 20 billion dollars and filed confidentially for an IPO. Corporate base listed in Cheyenne, Wyoming, with San Francisco origins. Well known in the crypto community and active in sports partnerships, including Williams Racing, Tottenham and others.

Lendbuzz is an AI-based auto financing company serving borrowers with thin or no credit histories, notably immigrants, by assessing them using alternative data and lending for new and used vehicles through dealer partners. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts; founded 2015. Has funded billions in loans through securitisations and raised significant venture money. Filed for an IPO on Nasdaq in 2025. Niche lender brand with limited consumer visibility.

Midea Group is one of the world's largest home appliance makers, producing air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, kitchenware and robotics (KUKA), plus commercial HVAC and smart building technology. Brands include Midea, Toshiba appliances, Eureka and Clivet. Sells to consumers and businesses worldwide, with revenue near 50 billion dollars and 190,000 employees. Headquartered in Foshan, Guangdong; founded 1968. Listed in Shenzhen (000333) and Hong Kong (0300). Big consumer brand in Asia, with sports sponsorship, including football.

Mobility Global is an automotive data and technology company providing vehicle and consumer analytics, software and mobility insights to car makers, dealers and marketers. It is based in Centreville, Virginia. Funding is shown at around 2 billion dollars. No more specific products, ownership or scale are known to us with confidence. B2B brand. Limited public information - check before outreach.

Dutch semiconductor maker producing automotive processors, radar, secure identification chips, NFC for payments and passports, and industrial connectivity. Customers are carmakers, phone makers and equipment manufacturers, with revenue of around 12 billion dollars and about 34,000 employees. Headquartered in Eindhoven; spun out of Philips in 2006. Listed on Nasdaq (NXPI). B2B component brand with low consumer awareness but strong ties to automotive, including sports-car partnerships such as the Ferrari Formula 1 connection.

Franco-Italian semiconductor maker selling microcontrollers, sensors, power chips, silicon carbide devices and MEMS to carmakers and industrial and consumer electronics firms; Apple and Tesla are well-known customers. Revenue of about 13 to 17 billion dollars and roughly 50,000 employees. Legal seat in Geneva (Plan-les-Ouates), operations in Italy and France; formed in 1987 by SGS and Thomson. Listed in Paris, Milan and New York (STM). B2B component brand with low consumer awareness, though it has sponsored motorsport and Formula E.

Verisure is a European provider of professionally monitored alarm systems for homes and small businesses, sold under Verisure and Securitas Direct brands across 18 countries, in Europe and Latin America. Earns subscription income from millions of customers. Headquartered in Versoix near Geneva, Switzerland; owned by private equity firm Hellman and Friedman (since 2021 with Temasek and others) and moved toward a 2025 IPO on Euronext Amsterdam (VRSR). Well known consumer brand in Spain, France and Nordic countries with significant advertising, including sponsorships.

Canadian financial technology company offering consumer investing, trading, crypto, tax filing, chequing and savings accounts and managed portfolios through the Wealthsimple app. Targets mainly younger Canadians, with over 3 million clients and tens of billions of Canadian dollars in assets. Headquartered in Toronto; launched 2014 as part of Power Corporation's group. Private, valued at 10 billion Canadian dollars after a 2025 funding round. Strong Canadian consumer brand with heavy advertising, previous sports and team partnerships.

Wheels Up is a US private aviation company offering jet card memberships, charter flights, fractional-style access and aircraft management using its own and partner fleets of light, midsize and large jets. Customers are corporates and wealthy individuals. Headquartered in New York; founded 2013. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (UP) via a 2021 SPAC merger, with Delta Air Lines as a major shareholder, and had a rescue financing in 2024. Known in the private flying market, with sports and events partnerships.

Australian buy now pay later fintech giving consumers instalment credit through Zip Pay and Zip Money at online and in-store retailers in Australia, New Zealand and, importantly, the United States, where it is the main growth market. Earns merchant and customer fees, with millions of users and thousands of merchants. Headquartered in Sydney; founded 2013. Listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ZIP). Recognised consumer finance brand in Australia and growing in the US, and has used sports partnerships.

German-headquartered global online food and quick-commerce delivery group, operating Talabat, Glovo, Foodpanda, Baemin (Woowa), PedidosYa, HungerStation and Yemeksepeti across about 70 countries in Asia, the Middle East, Europe and Latin America. Earns commissions, delivery fees and advertising from restaurants, retailers and consumers, with annual orders in the billions. Headquartered in Berlin; founded 2011. Listed in Frankfurt (DHER). Strong local consumer brands in many markets, although the group name itself is B2B; active in sports and event sponsorship.

Swiss dermatology company producing injectable aesthetics (Restylane, Dysport, Sculptra), dermatological skincare (Cetaphil, Differin, Benzac) and prescription treatments. Customers are dermatologists, healthcare professionals and consumers through pharmacies, with sales near 4 to 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland; operations in 90 countries. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (GALD) after a 2024 IPO, with EQT and ADIA as leading shareholders. Cetaphil is a widely recognised consumer skincare brand.

North American beverage company formed in 2018, combining Keurig Green Mountain coffee brewers and K-Cups with Dr Pepper Snapple's soft drinks, including Dr Pepper, 7UP, Canada Dry, Snapple, A&W and Core, and the acquisition of GHOST energy drinks. Sells to consumers through retailers and foodservice, with revenue near 15 billion dollars. Headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts and Frisco, Texas. Listed on Nasdaq (KDP), with JAB Holding a major holder; it announced a 2025 plan to acquire JDE Peet's. Strong US consumer brands.

World's largest beauty company, owning L'Oreal Paris, Lancome, Maybelline, Garnier, Kiehl's, Urban Decay, YSL Beaute, Kerastase, CeraVe and La Roche-Posay across consumer, luxury, dermatological and professional divisions. Sells cosmetics, hair and skincare to consumers worldwide, with sales above 40 billion euros and about 90,000 employees. Headquartered in Clichy, near Paris; founded 1909. Listed on Euronext Paris (OR), with the Bettencourt Meyers family and Nestle as shareholders. Hugely visible consumer brand with global ambassadors and sport and event sponsorship.

China's leading local services platform, running food delivery (Meituan Waimai and Keeta abroad), restaurant reviews, hotel and travel booking, instant retail, group buying and bike sharing. Earns commissions and advertising from merchants, with hundreds of millions of annual transacting users and revenue above 40 billion dollars. Headquartered in Beijing; founded 2010. Listed in Hong Kong (3690), with Tencent as a major shareholder. Everyday super-app for Chinese consumers, expanding into the Middle East and Brazil.

Japanese internet conglomerate running the Rakuten Ichiba marketplace, Rakuten Card and Bank, Rakuten Mobile, Rakuten Travel, Viber, Rakuten Kobo and Rakuten Securities. Serves consumers and merchants mostly in Japan, with a membership ecosystem of around 100 million, and revenue above 2 trillion yen. Headquartered in Tokyo; founded 1997 by Hiroshi Mikitani. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (4755). Strong consumer brand and an established sports sponsor (FC Barcelona and Golden State Warriors in the past, Vissel Kobe owner).

Cruise company operating Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea, plus a stake in TUI Cruises, with more than 65 ships and private destinations such as Perfect Day at CocoCay. Sells cruise vacations to consumers through travel agents and direct bookings, with revenue near 16 billion dollars. Headquartered in Miami, Florida; founded 1968. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RCL). Strong consumer brands in the US and Europe, with a history of sports sponsorship and marketing partnerships.

French hospitality group operating or franchising about 5,700 hotels in 110 countries under brands such as Sofitel, Pullman, Novotel, Mercure, Ibis, Fairmont, Raffles, Swissotel, Mövenpick and the Ennismore lifestyle brands, plus ALL loyalty and sport venue naming. Earns management and franchise fees. Headquartered in Issy-les-Moulineaux near Paris. Listed on Euronext Paris (AC), with Saudi PIF-linked Kingdom Holding a significant shareholder. Established consumer brands and an experienced sports sponsor, including Paris venue and football partnerships.

Online marketplace for short-term home rentals and experiences, connecting hosts with travellers in more than 220 countries and regions, with millions of listings. Earns service fees from guests and hosts, with revenue around 12 billion dollars and over 4 billion guest arrivals since founding. Headquartered in San Francisco; founded 2008. Listed on Nasdaq (ABNB) since its 2020 IPO. Globally recognised consumer brand, and a past Olympic and Paralympic sponsor and partner of major sports and events.

Second-largest US grocery chain, operating about 2,200 stores with 1,700 pharmacies under banners including Safeway, Albertsons, Vons, Jewel-Osco, Shaw's and Acme, plus the Signature Select private-label range. Customers are everyday shoppers, and it earns grocery, pharmacy and fuel revenue of near 80 billion dollars. Headquartered in Boise, Idaho; roughly 280,000 employees. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ACI). Its planned merger with Kroger was blocked in December 2024. Well-known US supermarket banners.

Canadian convenience store and fuel retailer operating Circle K, Couche-Tard and Ingo, with around 17,000 stores in 29 countries across North America, Europe and Asia. Sells fuel, fast food and everyday items to consumers, with revenue near 70 billion dollars. Headquartered in Laval, Quebec; founded 1980. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ATD). It pursued a 2025 bid for Seven & i, which later was withdrawn. Circle K is a very recognisable consumer brand and a past motorsport sponsor.

Italian world leader in hearing care retail, running about 10,000 shops under Amplifon, Miracle-Ear, NHS-affiliated and Elite Hearing brands in 26 countries, offering audiology services and hearing aids. Customers are people with hearing loss, mainly older consumers, with revenue near 2.3 billion euros. Headquartered in Milan; founded 1950. Listed on the Italian stock exchange (AMP). Known consumer brand in healthcare, and a sponsor of sports, such as AC Milan and Formula Racing.

British luxury sports car manufacturer producing the DB12, Vantage, DBX SUV, Valhalla and Valkyrie, sold to wealthy collectors through dealers. Makes cars at Gaydon and St Athan, with sales of around 6,000 units and revenue near 1.5 billion pounds, typically loss-making. Headquartered in Gaydon, Warwickshire; founded 1913. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (AML), with Lawrence Stroll's consortium and Saudi PIF as large shareholders. Iconic consumer brand and a Formula 1 works team (Aston Martin Aramco) since 2021.

Global travel retail and food service group, created by the 2023 merger of Dufry and Autogrill, operating duty-free and convenience shops (Dufry, Hudson, Duty Free) and restaurants in airports, railway stations, motorway services and cruise ships in 70 countries. Revenue near 14 billion Swiss francs from travelling consumers. Headquartered in Basel. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (AVOL). Visible to travellers as airport retail brands, with limited stand-alone brand awareness.

Switzerland-based world's largest chocolate and cocoa product maker, supplying industrial and artisan chocolatiers, bakeries, food manufacturers and restaurants with chocolate, cocoa and fillings under Callebaut, Cacao Barry and Van Houten. Revenue near 8 billion Swiss francs and about 13,000 employees in over 30 countries. Headquartered in Zurich; formed in 1996. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (BARN), with Jacobs Holding and Renata Coray related interests. B2B ingredient supplier with limited consumer brand awareness, though its brands are professional favourites.

BlueOval SK is a joint venture between Ford Motor Company and South Korea's SK On producing EV batteries for Ford and Lincoln vehicles at plants in Kentucky and Tennessee. In 2025 the partners announced they would split the venture, with Ford taking the Kentucky plants and SK On the Tennessee site. Reported investment is multiple billions of dollars, with a US government loan of about 9.6 billion dollars. B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand and limited sponsorship relevance.

US energy delivery company operating electric transmission and distribution in Houston area, plus natural gas distribution in Texas, Indiana, Ohio, Minnesota and Mississippi. Customers are millions of residential and commercial utility users, with revenue of roughly 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Houston, Texas. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CNP). Regulated utility with regional recognition, and known for being the electricity provider for Houston and an occasional local sports sponsor, but no wide consumer reach.

US food company known for Greek yogurt, also selling oat milk, creamers, coffee drinks, kefir and probiotics. Founded in 2005 by Hamdi Ulukaya, with its largest facilities in New Berlin, New York and Twin Falls, Idaho, and revenue near 3 billion dollars plus. Sells through supermarkets across the US and abroad. Privately held, with TPG and others as investors; raised large capital in 2025 at a valuation of 20 billion dollars. Strong consumer brand and a sponsor of US Olympic and Paralympic teams.

Networking hardware, software and services company, supplying optical and packet networking gear used by telecom carriers, cloud providers, governments and enterprises to move data over fiber, including coherent optics (WaveLogic) and Blue Planet software. Revenue near 4 billion dollars. Headquartered in Hanover, Maryland; founded 1992. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CIEN). B2B brand with low public visibility, but well known in telecom circles.

French food and beverage group making dairy and plant-based products, specialised nutrition and water, with brands like Activia, Actimel, Alpro, Danonino, Evian, Volvic, Oikos, Silk and baby formula brands Aptamil and Nutricia. Sells to consumers through retail worldwide in more than 120 markets, with revenue near 27 billion euros and about 90,000 employees. Headquartered in Paris; founded 1919. Listed on Euronext Paris (BN). Very strong consumer brands and a regular sports sponsor (Evian and Volvic in sport).

New England energy delivery company that transmits and distributes electricity and natural gas, and water distribution in Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire, serving around 4.5 million customers, including offshore wind ventures. Revenue near 12 billion dollars. Headquartered in Hartford, Connecticut and Boston. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ES). Regulated utility with regional brand recognition, and a local sponsor of New England sports.

Online travel group operating Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz, Travelocity, Wotif and the B2B Expedia Partner Solutions, selling flights, hotels, vacation rentals and packages to travellers worldwide. Earns commissions and advertising, with gross bookings above 100 billion dollars and revenue near 13 billion dollars. Headquartered in Seattle, Washington; spun out of Microsoft in 1996. Listed on Nasdaq (EXPE), with Liberty Expedia and Barry Diller's family as major shareholders. Widely known consumer travel brands with marketing and sports partnerships.

US-based global courier and logistics company running FedEx Express, Ground and Freight services, along with supply chain, e-commerce and customs solutions, delivering packages to over 220 countries with revenue near 88 billion dollars and 500,000 employees. Customers are consumers, shippers and enterprises. Headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee; founded 1971 by Fred Smith. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FDX), with a freight spin-off planned for 2026. Very strong B2B and consumer brand, with extensive sponsorship history including NASCAR, NFL and Formula 1.

US video game and collectibles retailer selling new and pre-owned games, consoles, accessories, trading cards and toys through about 3,000 stores in the US and a few other countries, and online. Revenue near 4 billion dollars. Headquartered in Grapevine, Texas; founded 1984. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (GME), famous for the meme stock surge of January 2021 and now holding sizeable cash and bitcoin investments. Well-known consumer retail brand among gamers and retail investors.

Canadian non-prime consumer lender and lease provider operating easyfinancial (personal and home equity loans), easyhome (lease-to-own furniture and electronics) and LendCare (point-of-sale financing). Serves Canadians with limited credit access through branches and online, with a loan book near 4 billion Canadian dollars. Headquartered in Mississauga, Ontario; founded 1990. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (GSY). Known in Canada as a financial services brand and has used sports sponsorship, such as Canadian sports and Formula 1 related campaigns.

Car rental company operating Hertz, Dollar and Thrifty brands at airports and city locations in North America, Europe and elsewhere, and renting to leisure and business travellers plus Firefly, and it has used EVs including Tesla in its fleet. Revenue near 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Estero, Florida; founded 1918. Listed on Nasdaq (HTZ), emerged from 2021 bankruptcy with Knighthead and Certares as large holders. Major consumer travel brand with a long motorsport and sports marketing record.

Timeshare and vacation ownership company selling points-based membership at resorts under Hilton Grand Vacations, Diamond Resorts and Bluegreen, operating more than 150 properties in the US, Europe, Asia and the Caribbean, with about 700,000 owner families. Earns from sales, financing and management fees, with revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Orlando, Florida; spun off from Hilton in 2017. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HGV). Consumer brand tied to Hilton.

US quick-service restaurant chain with about 2,200 Jack in the Box locations in several states, mostly California and Texas, known for tacos, burgers and late-night menus, and it owned Del Taco, acquired in 2022. Sells to consumers through franchisees, with revenue near 1.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in San Diego, California; founded 1951. Listed on Nasdaq (JACK). Del Taco divestiture was announced in 2025. Regional fast-food brand with strong awareness in the West and South.

World's largest meat company, processing beef, pork, chicken and lamb and selling under Seara, Swift, Friboi, Pilgrim's Pride, Moy Park and Primo Foods brands as well as plant-based Vivera. Customers are retailers, food service and consumers in over 190 countries, with revenue near 70 to 80 billion dollars. Headquartered in Sao Paulo, Brazil; founded 1953 by the Batista family, who control it. It listed on the New York Stock Exchange (JBS) in 2025, with a Brazilian listing too. Mostly B2B, with consumer brands in some markets, and a past sponsor of football and sports.

Europe's largest frozen food company owning Birds Eye, Findus and iglo, selling frozen fish, vegetables, poultry, ready meals and pizza to consumers through supermarkets in the UK, Italy, Germany, France, Sweden and elsewhere, with revenue near 3.3 billion euros. Headquartered in Woking, Surrey; formed in 2014 and previously known as Iglo Group. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NOMD) and has the London Stock Exchange listing. Familiar consumer brands, especially Birds Eye in the UK.

Cruise operator, part of Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings that also owns Oceania Cruises and Regent Seven Seas Cruises. NCL runs around 20 ships with 'Freestyle Cruising' and sells cruise vacations to consumers via travel advisers and online, and a private island Great Stirrup Cay. The group has revenue near 9.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Miami, Florida; founded 1966. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NCLH). Well-known cruise brand in the US and Europe, with some sports sponsorship.

Olam Food Ingredients is the food and beverage ingredients business of Olam Group, supplying cocoa, coffee, dairy, nuts and spices to food manufacturers and retailers. Customers are food and beverage producers worldwide, with the coffee and cocoa lines among the largest globally. Headquartered in Singapore; Olam Group is majority owned by Singapore's Temasek. ofi was set up in 2022 as a separate business within Olam and has been preparing for a separate listing. B2B ingredient supplier with limited consumer awareness.

US lodging real estate investment trust owning about 40 upscale and luxury hotels in leading urban and resort markets, including Hilton Hawaiian Village, Hilton Chicago and Casa Marina, mostly operated by Hilton, Hyatt and Marriott brands. Earns room and hospitality revenue, with over 2.5 billion dollars annual revenue. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia; spun off from Hilton in 2017. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (PK). Property owner, not a consumer brand, with guests booking under Hilton or Hyatt names.

One of the world's largest chicken producers, with processing plants in the United States, Mexico, the UK and Europe, making fresh and prepared chicken and pork sold to retailers and food service customers, and under brands such as Pilgrim's, Just Bare and Moy Park. Revenue near 17 billion dollars. Headquartered in Greeley, Colorado; founded 1946. Listed on Nasdaq (PPC) and majority controlled by JBS. A familiar food brand in the US supermarket aisle, with sponsorship through events such as NASCAR.

Consumer packaged goods holding company with brands in cereal (Post Consumer Brands, Honey Bunches of Oats, Pebbles, Malt-O-Meal), refrigerated foods (Michael Foods, Bob Evans), foodservice and pet food (Nutrish and Nutro acquired from Smucker's) and more. Customers include grocery stores, restaurants and consumers across North America and Europe, with revenue near 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in St Louis, Missouri; spun out of Ralcorp in 2012. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (POST). Well-known US cereal brands.

US real estate investment trust owning large convention and entertainment hotels operated by Marriott, such as Gaylord Opryland in Nashville, Gaylord Texan, Gaylord Palms, Gaylord National, plus the Grand Ole Opry and the Ole Red venues. Earns hospitality revenue from group business and entertainment, near 2.3 billion dollars. Headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RHP). Strong destination brands in Nashville, though a niche brand to wider consumers.

Indian food delivery and quick-commerce platform operating Swiggy food delivery, Instamart grocery, Dineout and Genie services, with Swiggy One loyalty. Earns commissions, delivery fees and advertising from restaurants, brands and consumers, in over 500 cities. Headquartered in Bengaluru; founded 2014. Listed on the NSE and BSE (SWIGGY) since its November 2024 IPO. Big consumer app in India with heavy advertising and cricket sponsorship, competing with Zomato (Eternal).

Online retail and technology group owning beauty brands (LookFantastic, Cult Beauty, Dermstore), nutrition (Myprotein, Myvegan), and the THG Ingenuity technology platform that powers e-commerce for other brands. Customers are consumers in 160-plus countries and brand partners, with revenue near 2 billion pounds. Headquartered in Manchester, England; founded 2004 by Matthew Moulding as The Hut Group. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (THG) since 2020. Myprotein and LookFantastic are strong consumer brands, with sports and athlete partnerships.

Travel and Leisure Co. is a timeshare and travel club company running the Wyndham Destinations vacation ownership business, Club Wyndham, WorldMark and the Travel + Leisure membership and magazine brand, plus Panorama exchange via RCI. Customers are vacation owners and members, with revenue near 4 billion dollars. Headquartered in Orlando, Florida; spun out of Wyndham in 2018. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TNL). Consumer travel brand known through the Travel + Leisure name.

Wonder is a US food and mealtime company that operates food halls, restaurant brands and meal delivery from Wonder, led by founder Marc Lore, and acquired Grubhub in 2025. Offers multi-restaurant ordering with chef-driven concepts via trucks and mobile kitchens in the New Jersey and New York region. Funding in the input is around 3.2 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York. Growing but emerging consumer brand in the US Northeast, with a lot of media attention.

Luxury integrated resort and casino operator running Wynn Las Vegas and Encore in Nevada, Wynn Macau and Wynn Palace in Macau, plus a new Wynn Al Marjan Island resort being built in the UAE (Ras Al Khaimah). Customers are high-end gamblers, leisure guests and event attendees, with revenue near 7 billion dollars. Headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada; founded by Steve Wynn in 2002. Listed on Nasdaq (WYNN). Strong luxury casino brand globally and a partner in Formula 1 Las Vegas events.

One of China's largest express delivery companies, running a partner network of franchise outlets and transit centres that handle more than 30 billion parcels a year for e-commerce shippers (Taobao, Pinduoduo, JD). Revenue near 5 to 6 billion dollars. Headquartered in Shanghai; founded 2002. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ZTO) and in Hong Kong (2057). Known to Chinese e-commerce shoppers as a parcel brand, but it has limited recognition outside China.

US digital financial services company providing auto loans and leases through dealers, online banking, mortgage, corporate finance and insurance (Ally Bank), with around 11 million customers. Revenue near 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Detroit, Michigan; formerly GMAC, rebranded Ally in 2010. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ALLY). Familiar US consumer finance brand with significant advertising, and an experience in motorsport sponsorship, including NASCAR and IndyCar.

Swedish-American automotive safety supplier, the world's largest maker of airbags, seatbelts and steering wheels for car makers, with sales near 10.5 billion dollars and about 65,000 employees at plants in 25 countries. Customers are global car companies. Legal headquarters in Stockholm, Sweden, with operations managed from Auburn Hills, Michigan; formed in 1997 by the merger of Autoliv and Morton ASP. Listed in Stockholm (ALIV SDB) and the New York Stock Exchange (ALV). B2B, limited consumer visibility.

Fisker Inc. was a California-based electric vehicle maker that sold the Ocean SUV, an EV built by Magna Steyr in Austria, and planned further models. Founded by designer Henrik Fisker, it listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FSR) via a SPAC in 2020. After production problems and financing failure, it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in June 2024, with assets later sold and Ocean owners' servicing contested. Defunct. Brief consumer awareness but now not a viable sponsor.

Diversified holding company controlled by activist investor Carl Icahn, with segments including Investment, Energy (CVR Energy), Automotive (Pep Boys and Icahn Automotive), Food Packaging (Viskase), Real Estate, Home Fashion (WestPoint) and Pharma. Customers vary by business, from refinery buyers to car-service consumers. Headquartered in Sunny Isles Beach, Florida. Listed on Nasdaq (IEP), a master limited partnership. Parent has low direct consumer recognition, though Pep Boys carries local awareness.

Swedish premium carmaker producing Volvo vehicles, with models such as the XC90, XC60, EX30 and EX90, known for safety. Sells about 700,000 cars a year to consumers worldwide with revenue near 400 billion Swedish kronor. Headquartered in Gothenburg; founded 1927 (Volvo Cars separate from AB Volvo trucks since 1999). Controlled by China's Geely Holding and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (VOLCAR B). Strong consumer brand and a past Formula E and sports sponsor.

Zhiji Auto, known as IM Motors, is a Shanghai-based premium electric vehicle brand jointly backed by SAIC Motor, Zhangjiang Hi-Tech and Alibaba, selling IM L6, LS6 and LS7 smart EVs, including solid-state battery ambitions. It sells to consumers mainly in China and has started expanding in Europe. Raised about 12 billion yuan in funding. Mid-market consumer awareness in China, growing, supported by Alibaba's technology and SAIC's manufacturing.

FAW Pentium (Bestune) is a Chinese passenger car brand under state-owned FAW Group, selling sedans and SUVs such as the T77, T99 and NAT electric models mainly to consumers in China, with some exports. Based in Changchun, Jilin, where FAW is headquartered; Pentium started as a Mazda-based licensed model. Funding listed is about 10.9 billion yuan. Established mid-market domestic brand in China, with limited recognition abroad.

IONITY is a European high-power charging network operator for electric vehicles, with over 5,000 charging points at about 800 sites across 25 countries, serving drivers from partners including BMW, Ford, Hyundai Kia, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen and Stellantis, and with a new investment partner BlackRock. Established 2017 as a joint venture of car manufacturers. Headquartered in Munich. Privately held. Recognisable to EV drivers in Europe; its stations are on motorways, not consumer retail, and it has done motorsport marketing.

French automaker selling Renault, Dacia and Alpine cars and light commercial vehicles, with models such as the Clio, Captur, Megane E-Tech, Duster and Sandero, and a financing arm RCI Banque. Sells nearly 2.3 million vehicles a year with revenue near 56 billion euros. Headquartered in Boulogne-Billancourt near Paris; founded 1899. Listed on Euronext Paris (RNO), with the French state and Nissan as large shareholders, a reorganised Alliance with Nissan. Strong consumer brand and Formula 1 history through Alpine.

German technology supplier of transmissions, chassis, driver assistance, electric drive and commercial vehicle systems, with sales near 40 billion euros and about 160,000 employees in around 30 countries. Customers are global car, truck and rail makers. Headquartered in Friedrichshafen; founded 1915 as Zahnradfabrik. Owned by the Zeppelin Foundation (majority) and Dr Jurgen and Irmgard Ulderup Foundation, so unlisted. Restructuring in 2024 and 2025 with job cuts. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness, though it is a visible motorsport sponsor, including Formula 1 and Sauber links.

Electra is a French operator of ultra-fast electric vehicle charging stations in France, Belgium, Italy and other countries, with a pay-as-you-go app and subscription. Founded 2020 by Aurelien Ranaud, backed by Eurazeo, EDF and Mitsubishi and others; funding is about 789 million euros including debt. Headquartered in Paris. Planned to deploy thousands of fast-charging points. Known to EV drivers in France, with limited broader consumer awareness.

Erisha E Mobility is an Indian electric vehicle manufacturer based in New Delhi, said by Crunchbase to provide electric vehicles. The input does not provide the product lines, customer segments, scale or ownership, and funding is shown as about 1 billion dollars. Limited public information - check before outreach.

First Brands Group is a US automotive aftermarket parts maker whose brands include Fram filters, Autolite spark plugs, Trico wipers, Raybestos brakes, Luk clutches and Carter fuel systems. Sells through retailers such as AutoZone and Advance, and to installers. Headquartered in Rochester Hills, Michigan; owned by Patrick James and private equity. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2025 amid financing controversies involving off-balance-sheet debt. Consumer-facing brand names are well known to car owners, such as Fram.

GridServe is a UK company operating the GridServe Electric Highway fast charging network on motorways and its flagship electric forecourts, along with solar and battery farms and electric vehicle subscription services. Founded 2017 by Toddington Harper, backed by large investment rounds. Taken on the former Electric Highway motorway service contract with Ecotricity. Visible to EV drivers in the UK, with limited wider public brand recognition.

Lithia & Driveway is the third-largest US auto retailer by revenue, operating over 400 franchised stores in the US, Canada and the UK, selling new and used cars, parts and service and finance, plus its Driveway online sales and Pfaff and GreenCars brands. Revenue is near 37 billion dollars. Headquartered in Medford, Oregon; founded 1946. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (LAD). Local dealer brands are known regionally, and Driveway is its national digital brand.

XCMG Automobile is the automotive division of XCMG Group, one of the world's largest construction machinery makers, producing heavy trucks, special-purpose vehicles and truck mixers in China. Based in Xuzhou, Jiangsu, and state-linked via the group. Funding listed is about 6.4 billion yuan. B2B commercial vehicle maker with little consumer awareness outside China, though XCMG as a group is a visible name in construction equipment.

Copeland is a climate technology company making compressors, controls and software for heating, cooling and refrigeration, including the Scroll and Copeland-brand compressors used in HVAC and cold chain systems. Sells to equipment makers and contractors worldwide.
