Headquartered in St Louis, Missouri (with operations in Sidney, Ohio); formerly Emerson's Climate Technologies, sold in 2023 to Blackstone in a deal that valued the business at about 14 billion dollars, with Emerson retaining a stake. B2B brand with low consumer awareness; the input's consumer electronics tag is inaccurate.

Foxconn Technology Group, formally Hon Hai Precision Industry, is the world's largest electronics contract manufacturer, assembling iPhones for Apple and servers, including for Nvidia AI, as well as electric vehicles through Foxtron and EV platforms. Revenue near 200 billion dollars and over 1 million employees, with plants in China, India, Vietnam, Mexico and the US. Headquartered in New Taipei City; founded 1974 by Terry Gou. Listed in Taipei (2317). B2B manufacturer, little consumer brand awareness.

Payments company operating the Epay prepaid top-up, Ria money transfer and Euronet ATM and card processing businesses, plus the Dandelion network, moving money and digital value across 200 countries. Customers are consumers sending remittances, banks, mobile operators and retailers, with revenue near 4 billion dollars. Headquartered in Leawood, Kansas; founded 1994. Listed on Nasdaq (EEFT). Ria is a recognised remittance brand in migrant communities, with some sports sponsorship.

World Liberty Financial is a cryptocurrency and decentralised finance project linked to the Trump family, offering the WLFI governance token and the USD1 stablecoin. Launched in September 2024 and promoted by Donald Trump and his sons, with large token sales, including to investors from Asia. The input shows the company registered in Wilmington, Delaware and around 1.9 billion dollars in funding. Controversial political profile and substantial name recognition, though regulatory scrutiny, and political sensitivity affect sponsorship suitability.

ElectroMobility Poland is a Polish state-owned company created in 2016 to develop the Izera electric car brand and build a factory in Jaworzno, Silesia, with a platform from Geely. Owned by Polish state energy and industry companies including PGE, Enea, Energa and Tauron. Planned launch of Izera cars has been repeatedly delayed. Funding listed is about 4.5 billion zloty. Headquartered in Warsaw. Brand is more of a national project than a known consumer name.

Taiwanese maker of Smartscooters and a battery-swapping network (GoStation) serving electric scooter riders in Taiwan, with expansion to India, China, Japan and Southeast Asia and partnerships with Yamaha, Suzuki and Hero MotoCorp. Earns from scooter sales, battery subscriptions and swapping fees, with hundreds of thousands of riders. Headquartered in Taipei; founded 2011. Listed on Nasdaq (GGR) via a 2022 SPAC deal. Popular urban electric scooter brand in Taiwan with limited global recognition.

Aeva Technologies develops 4D lidar sensors using frequency-modulated continuous-wave technology that measure distance and velocity for automated driving, industrial and consumer uses. Customers include Daimler Truck, with partners such as LG Innotek and Airbus. Headquartered in Mountain View, California; founded 2016 by former Apple engineers. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (AEVA) since a 2021 SPAC merger. B2B technology company with very little public awareness.

Empery Digital is a US Nasdaq-listed company (EMPD) formerly called Volcon, which made electric off-road powersports vehicles, and in 2025 pivoted to a bitcoin treasury strategy. Based in Round Rock, Texas. Crunchbase describes it as an off-road powersports company. Funding shown at around 723 million dollars looks unusually high for the business, so check before use. Small cap with little consumer awareness.

OPENLANE, formerly KAR Auction Services, runs digital wholesale used-vehicle marketplaces (OPENLANE, TradeRev, ADESA digital) and finance services (AFC), connecting dealers, fleets and manufacturers. Sold its physical ADESA auctions to Carvana in 2022. Revenue near 1.9 billion dollars. Headquartered in Carmel, Indiana, with the input showing Kansas City, Missouri. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (OPLN). B2B marketplace brand, little consumer awareness.

Power Solutions International makes emissions-certified engines and power systems running on natural gas, propane and other fuels for industrial equipment, forklifts, generators and on-road vehicles, along with engine management. Customers are equipment manufacturers in the US and abroad. Headquartered in Wood Dale, Illinois; listed on Nasdaq (PSIX). Revenue near 450 million dollars. B2B supplier with minimal consumer brand awareness.

Slate Auto is a US startup building a low-cost electric pickup that can be customised with body kits, backed by Jeff Bezos and Bezos Expeditions, with a Warsaw, Indiana factory for production starting in late 2026. Founded 2022, a Re:Build manufacturing spin-out; the input shows Troy, Michigan. Raised about 760 million dollars. Prices are said to start around 27,000 dollars before incentives. Still pre-production but has drawn a very large number of reservations and media attention.

Constellium is a global aluminium products maker producing rolled and extruded aluminium for aerospace, automotive and packaging, such as sheet for beverage cans and car body parts. Customers are industrial manufacturers, with revenue near 7 billion euros and about 12,000 employees. Headquartered in Paris with executive teams in Baltimore and Zurich; formed in 2011 from Alcan's engineered products. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CSTM) and Euronext Paris. B2B manufacturer with little consumer awareness.

Dealer Tire helps automotive manufacturers and dealerships with tires, wheels and related products and services, according to Crunchbase, which tags it under automotive and industrial categories. It is headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio. Funding shown in the input is about 658 million dollars. The input does not give product lines, customer scale, ownership or founding details. Limited public information - check before outreach.

Dutch operator of fast charging stations for electric cars, with solar roofed stations across the Netherlands, Germany, the UK, Belgium, France, Denmark and Switzerland, serving thousands of drivers through its app and the pay-as-you-go model. Financed by retail investors via a crowd-funding structure, unusual in the sector. Headquartered in Amsterdam; founded 2012. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam (FAST). Known mainly to EV drivers in Europe.

GreenCell Mobility is an Indian electric bus operator serving public transport authorities in cities such as Delhi and Mumbai, under gross cost contracts for clean urban transit, with a fleet of electric buses. Headquartered in Mumbai; part of the Greencell Express group, supported by investors including Macquarie Asia Infrastructure Fund. Funding shown at around 625 million dollars. B2G service operator with low consumer brand awareness.

Japanese carmaker producing Subaru vehicles such as the Impreza, Forester, Outback, Crosstrek, WRX and BRZ, known for symmetrical all-wheel drive and boxer engines, along with aerospace products. Sells about 900,000 cars a year to consumers, mostly in North America. Headquartered in Tokyo; formerly Fuji Heavy Industries, renamed 2017. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (7270), with Toyota a major shareholder. Strong consumer brand in the US with a history in rallying and a long-time sponsor of sports.

Textainer Group Holdings is one of the largest lessors of intermodal shipping containers, leasing standard dry containers and refrigerated containers to shipping lines worldwide. Headquartered in San Francisco, California, with an origin in Bermuda. It was acquired by Stonepeak, the private equity infrastructure investor, in a deal announced in 2024 for about 7.4 billion dollars in enterprise value, and delisted from the New York Stock Exchange (TGH). B2B leasing company with no consumer awareness.

World's largest cruise company, operating Carnival Cruise Line, Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Seabourn, P&O Cruises, Cunard, Costa Cruises and AIDA with around 90 ships. Sells cruise holidays to millions of consumers a year, with revenue near 25 billion dollars. Headquartered in Miami, Florida, with Carnival plc in the UK; founded 1972. Dual listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CCL) and London (CCL). Very strong consumer brands with sports and entertainment sponsorships.

Southeast Asia's leading super app, offering ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery (GrabFood), digital payments and financial services (GrabPay), across eight countries including Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia and Vietnam. Earns commissions, advertising and financial fees, with about 40 million monthly users. Headquartered in Singapore; founded 2012 in Malaysia. Listed on Nasdaq (GRAB) since its 2021 SPAC merger. Strong consumer brand across Southeast Asia and a Formula 1 sponsor (Grab as a title sponsor of the Singapore Grand Prix).

World's largest temperature-controlled warehousing and logistics provider, with over 400 cold storage facilities across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, storing and transporting food for retailers, producers and distributors. Revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Novi, Michigan; founded 2008. Listed on Nasdaq (LINE) after a record 2024 IPO of about 4.4 billion dollars, with Bay Grove Capital and others as shareholders. B2B logistics brand with essentially no consumer awareness.

Digital payments company running the PayPal wallet, Venmo, Braintree, Xoom and Honey and the PYUSD stablecoin, with over 430 million active accounts. Earns from transaction fees on merchants and consumers and credit products, with revenue near 32 billion dollars. Headquartered in San Jose, California; founded 1998, spun out of eBay in 2015. Listed on Nasdaq (PYPL). One of the best-known payment brands in the world, with sports sponsorship, including Formula 1 partnerships and stadium naming.

Consumer Cellular is a US mobile virtual network operator selling prepaid-like wireless plans and phones, mainly to people over 50, via retail stores, AARP membership, and online, running on AT&T and T-Mobile networks. Headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona; formed 1995. Privately held; it was acquired by Kohlberg & Company in 2021. Customer service-focused brand with national TV advertising and strong awareness among older consumers.

Global beauty company in fragrance, cosmetics and skincare, with brands such as CoverGirl, Rimmel, Sally Hansen, Max Factor, Gucci, Burberry, Calvin Klein and Hugo Boss licences. Sells to consumers through department stores, mass retailers and online, with revenue near 5.9 billion dollars. Legal seat in Amsterdam, with offices in New York and Paris; founded 1904. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (COTY), with JAB Holding a large shareholder. Strong consumer brands and licence brands with sports tie-ins.

British premium spirits and beer company owning Johnnie Walker, Smirnoff, Guinness, Tanqueray, Don Julio, Captain Morgan, Baileys and Crown Royal, sold in about 180 countries with revenue near 20 billion dollars. Customers are consumers via retailers, bars and restaurants and e-commerce. Headquartered in London; formed in 1997 from Guinness and Grand Metropolitan. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (DGE) and New York (DEO). Very strong consumer brands and a major sports sponsor, including Formula 1 as an official global Formula 1 partner through Johnnie Walker and Guinness 0.0.

Prestige beauty company with brands including Estee Lauder, Clinique, MAC, La Mer, Bobbi Brown, Tom Ford Beauty, Jo Malone London, Aveda and Origins, selling skincare, makeup, fragrance and haircare in about 150 countries through department stores, travel retail and online. Revenue near 15 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York; founded 1946, still controlled by the Lauder family. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (EL). Very strong consumer brand, with Formula 1 and film partnerships.

UK sports, premium and luxury retail group owning Sports Direct, House of Fraser, Flannels, Evans Cycles, GAME and Jack Wills, and holding minority stakes in other retailers such as ASOS and Boohoo. Customers are consumers via stores and online, with revenue near 5.5 billion pounds. Headquartered in Shirebrook, Derbyshire (input shows London); led by Mike Ashley. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (FRAS). Mass-market sports retail brand in the UK and Europe.

One of the world's largest ice cream makers, producing brands under licence and in-house including Nestle brands under licence such as Drumstick and Maxibon, plus its own Mini Milk, Oreo and Cadbury ice cream licences and Cornetto-type novelties. Formed in 2016 as a joint venture of Nestle and PAI Partners. Sells to consumers through retailers in more than 20 countries, with revenue near 4 billion euros. Headquartered in Harrogate, North Yorkshire. Privately held. Corporate name little known; consumers know the product brands.

US real estate investment trust specialising in casino and gaming properties leased to operators including Penn Entertainment, Caesars and Boyd under long-term triple net leases. Earns rental income from about 60 properties and has expanded into other sectors. Headquartered in Wyomissing, Pennsylvania (input shows Palo Alto); spun off from Penn National in 2013. Listed on Nasdaq (GLPI). Landlord, not a consumer-facing brand.

Gopuff is a US instant delivery service for snacks, groceries, alcohol, personal care and household items from micro-fulfilment centres, with 15-minute-style delivery in many cities and a retail presence through BevMo, which it owns. Customers are consumers using the Gopuff app, and it has operated in the US and the UK and Ireland. Headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; founded 2013. Privately held with SoftBank and others as investors, valued at about 15 billion dollars in 2021. Known to US urban consumers, with a history of sports sponsorship.

Consumer health company spun out of Johnson & Johnson in 2023, owning Tylenol, Neutrogena, Aveeno, Listerine, Band-Aid, Johnson's baby care, Nicorette and Zyrtec. Sells to consumers via retailers worldwide, with revenue near 15 billion dollars. Headquartered in Summit, New Jersey. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (KVUE). In November 2025 it agreed to be acquired by Kimberly-Clark in a deal valued at about 48.7 billion dollars. Household consumer brands with extensive advertising.

India's largest online travel company, selling flights, hotels, buses, trains and holidays through MakeMyTrip, goibibo and redBus, with corporate travel services. Customers are Indian leisure and business travellers, plus expanding in the Middle East, with revenue near 900 million dollars. Operational base in Gurugram, Haryana; legal domicile in Mauritius; founded 2000. Listed on Nasdaq (MMYT), with Trip.com Group and Naspers/Prosus as major shareholders. Very well known consumer travel brand in India, and an active cricket and sports advertiser.

Indian hospitality technology company that signs up independent hotels and homes into a branded network (OYO Rooms, OYO Townhouse, Belvilla in Europe, and Oravel Stays), operating mainly in India, Southeast Asia, Europe and the US. Earns commissions and revenue share from hotels, with a large chain presence. Headquartered in Gurugram; founded 2013 by Ritesh Agarwal. Private (parent PRISM) backed by SoftBank, which cut its valuation sharply; a listing was planned. Widely recognised budget hotel brand in India.

French wine and spirits group owning Absolut, Jameson, Chivas Regal, Ballantine's, Martell, Havana Club, The Glenlivet, Beefeater, Malibu, Kahlua and Perrier-Jouet, sold in over 160 countries. Revenue near 11 billion euros and about 19,000 employees. Headquartered in Paris; formed in 1975 from Pernod and Ricard, with the Ricard family a large shareholder. Listed on Euronext Paris (RI). Very strong consumer brands and an active sponsor of sports and music.

US house of fashion brands owning Coach, Kate Spade New York and Stuart Weitzman (sold to Caleres in 2025), selling handbags, accessories, footwear and apparel to consumers through its own stores, e-commerce, wholesale and outlets in about 40 countries. Revenue near 7 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York; founded 1941 as Coach. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TPR). Its attempted acquisition of Capri Holdings was blocked in 2024. Strong consumer fashion brands.

The Magnum Ice Cream Company was demerged from Unilever in December 2025, owning Magnum, Wall's, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto, Algida, Klondike, Breyers and Talenti, selling frozen desserts to consumers through retailers and freezers in about 100 countries. Revenue near 8 billion euros. Headquartered in Amsterdam. Listed in Amsterdam, London and New York. Very strong consumer ice cream brands.

US restaurant franchise operator with KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and The Habit Burger & Grill, with over 60,000 restaurants in more than 155 countries and a heavily franchised model that earns royalties. Revenue near 7.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky; spun off from PepsiCo in 1997. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (YUM). Separate Yum China is a listed entity. Very strong consumer fast-food brands and long-standing sports sponsors, including Taco Bell's links with motorsport.

Operator of Upbit, South Korea's largest cryptocurrency exchange, plus the Lounge blockchain platform and related digital asset services. Customers are retail crypto traders in Korea and Southeast Asia, with revenue from trading fees. Headquartered in Seoul; founded 2012. Unlisted, with a planned merger into Naver Financial announced in late 2025 through a share swap valued around 10 trillion won. Strong consumer brand in Korean crypto and a sponsor in esports and entertainment.

South Korean internet group behind KakaoTalk, the dominant messenger used by most of the population, plus Kakao Pay, Kakao Bank, Kakao Mobility (taxi), Kakao Entertainment and Melon. Earns from advertising, commerce, fintech and content. Headquartered in Jeju, with main operations in Pangyo near Seoul; founded 2010. Listed on the Korea Exchange (035720). Everyday super-app brand in Korea with extensive consumer reach and mascot licensing (Kakao Friends).

South Korean maker of display panels, notably OLED and LCD screens for TVs, smartphones, monitors, laptops and cars, supplying LG Electronics, Apple, and automotive customers. Revenue near 20 trillion won. Headquartered in Seoul (Yeouido); established in 1985 as a joint venture, spun out in 1999 from LG. Listed on the Korea Exchange (034220) and New York (LPL), with LG Corp as the main shareholder. B2B component brand with limited consumer awareness.

Zipline designs, manufactures and operates autonomous delivery drones, which carry blood, medicines, groceries and food from fixed sites to homes and clinics. Started with medical deliveries in Rwanda and Ghana and now serves customers in the US, including Walmart and health systems. Headquartered in South San Francisco, California; founded 2014. Privately held with funding of about 2 billion dollars and a valuation above 4 billion dollars. Growing consumer visibility through retail partnerships.

AT&S is an Austrian maker of high-end printed circuit boards and IC substrates for smartphones, servers, AI chips and cars, with plants in Austria, China, India and Malaysia. Customers are major chip and electronics companies including Apple and Intel. Headquartered in Leoben, Styria; founded 1987. Listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange (ATS). B2B component brand, essentially no consumer awareness; the consumer electronics tag in the input is a loose fit.

Atome is a buy now pay later and consumer finance app operating in Southeast Asia, including Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, plus Hong Kong. Lets shoppers pay in instalments at partner merchants. Part of the Advance Intelligence Group, headquartered in Singapore, also known for AI risk tooling. Funding shown is about 1.5 billion dollars at group level. Consumer brand with strong awareness in the region.

Bitmine Immersion Technologies is a US-listed company, now run as an ether treasury company holding one of the largest corporate stashes of ETH, after earlier work on bitcoin mining with immersion cooling. Based in Las Vegas, Nevada, chaired by Tom Lee of Fundstrat. Traded on NYSE American (BMNR). Funding shown is about 1.5 billion dollars. Investor-facing business with little consumer awareness.

Capchase is a fintech that provides non-dilutive financing to software and subscription companies, advancing the money from annual contracts through products such as Capchase Grow. Customers are startups and SaaS businesses, plus a payments offering. Headquartered in New York; founded 2020 by Miguel Fernandez and Luis Basagoiti with offices in Spain. Raised around 1.3 billion dollars largely in debt and equity. B2B finance brand with low consumer awareness.

Columbus McKinnon designs and makes material handling equipment, such as hoists, cranes, chain, rigging and lifting products and intelligent motion control, serving industrial, entertainment, infrastructure and construction customers. Revenue near 1 billion dollars. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, with historic roots in Amherst, New York; founded 1875. Listed on Nasdaq (CMCO). B2B industrial brand with no consumer visibility, though its hoists are used in stage rigging.

FalconX is a digital asset prime broker offering trading, lending, custody and derivatives for crypto institutions such as funds, banks and miners, and acquired 21Shares in 2025. Founded 2018 by Raghu Yarlagadda and based in San Mateo, California. Raised about 1.5 billion dollars in funding and valued at 8 billion dollars. Privately held. Institutional B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

Hainan Airlines is a Chinese full-service airline founded in 1993 and based on Hainan island, a subsidiary of HNA group, now flagship of Hainan Airlines Holding under a 2021 restructuring led by Liaoning Fangda. Flies domestic and international routes from Haikou, Beijing and elsewhere, serving leisure and business travellers. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600221). Well-known Chinese carrier with a Skytrax five-star rating history.

VIAVI Solutions makes network test, measurement and assurance equipment and software for telecom carriers, data centers and cable operators, plus optical security and anti-counterfeiting coatings used on banknotes and in consumer electronics. Customers are network equipment makers, service providers and governments, with revenue near 1 billion dollars. Headquartered in Chandler, Arizona (formerly San Jose); spun out of JDS Uniphase in 2015. Listed on Nasdaq (VIAV). B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

Clip is a Mexican payments and commerce company known for its card-reader terminals and point of sale tools that let small businesses accept card payments, plus business loans and online payments. Customers are merchants of all sizes across Mexico. Headquartered in Mexico City; founded 2012. Venture backed with about 1.1 billion dollars raised including debt facilities. Private. Well known to small business owners in Mexico, with limited reach with consumers elsewhere.

Diodes Incorporated designs and supplies discrete, analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, including power management, protection and timing chips for automotive, industrial, computing, communications and consumer markets. Revenue near 1.3 billion dollars, with factories in Asia and the US. Headquartered in Plano, Texas; founded 1959. Listed on Nasdaq (DIOD). B2B component supplier with essentially no consumer awareness.

Global information services company offering credit reports and scores, fraud prevention, data analytics, marketing services and consumer credit tools such as Experian Boost and CreditWorks. Customers are lenders, retailers, businesses and consumers in about 30 countries, with revenue near 7 billion dollars and about 22,000 employees. Operational headquarters in Costa Mesa, California; Irish-domiciled parent Experian plc is based in Dublin. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (EXPN). Recognised credit bureau brand.

Forward Financing is a US alternative lender to small businesses, offering merchant cash advances, term loans and lines of credit that are repaid from daily sales. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts; founded 2012. Funded through capital partners with total funding shown at about 1.1 billion dollars. Customers are small retailers, restaurants and service firms. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness.

FundPark is a Hong Kong-based fintech providing supply chain and working capital financing to small and medium sized exporters and online sellers in Asia, using data and automation for credit decisions. Located in Kwun Tong, Kowloon; funding shown at about 1.1 billion dollars largely from debt facilities. Customers are SMEs. B2B finance brand with no meaningful consumer awareness. Limited public information - check before outreach.

ID Finance is a Spanish fintech lender using machine learning to offer online consumer loans and credit cards in Spain, Mexico, Brazil, Poland and the Philippines, through brands such as MoneyMan and Creditea. Customers are retail borrowers who apply by app. Headquartered in Barcelona; founded 2012. Private, with funding of about 900 million dollars including debt. Active marketing in consumer finance but little general brand recognition.

IIFL Home Finance is an Indian housing finance company, part of the IIFL group, offering home loans, loans against property and construction finance mainly to salaried and self-employed borrowers in smaller cities. Operates through a nationwide branch network. Headquartered in Gurugram, Haryana (the registered office is in Mumbai). Subsidiary of IIFL Finance, listed on the NSE and BSE, with funding shown at about 940 million dollars. Moderate brand awareness in India.

Lendo is a Saudi lending marketplace that connects SMEs and digital businesses with alternative finance, based in Riyadh. Offers working capital and receivable-backed financing and has been backed by regional funds. Funding shown at around 975 million dollars, including debt facilities. B2B fintech brand, with limited consumer awareness outside the Saudi startup scene. Limited public information - check before outreach.

Aligned Data Centers builds and operates large-scale data centers and cooling technology for cloud providers, AI developers and enterprises, with campuses in the US and Latin America. Headquartered in Plano, Texas; founded 2013. Agreed in 2025 to be acquired by the AI Infrastructure Partnership, a group including BlackRock, Nvidia, Microsoft and MGX, in a deal valued at about 40 billion dollars. B2B infrastructure brand with no consumer visibility.

Dollarama is Canada's largest dollar store chain, operating over 1,600 stores with fixed price points across all provinces, selling consumables, household goods and seasonal items to value-seeking shoppers, and owns a majority of Dollarcity in Latin America. Revenue near 7 billion Canadian dollars. Headquartered in Montreal (Mont-Royal); founded 1992. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (DOL). Well-known Canadian retail brand.

FTAI Aviation owns and leases commercial aircraft engines and parts and runs an engine maintenance and parts business, serving airlines worldwide. Revenue near 2.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York; spun out of Fortress Transportation and Infrastructure Investors in 2022 (infrastructure assets went to a separate company). Listed on Nasdaq (FTAI). B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Kimberly-Clark is a US consumer products company making Huggies diapers, Kleenex tissues, Cottonelle, Scott, Kotex and Depend, plus Kimberly-Clark Professional products, sold in 175 countries. Revenue near 20 billion dollars. Headquartered in Irving, Texas; founded 1872. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (KMB). In November 2025 it agreed to acquire Kenvue (Tylenol, Neutrogena) in a deal valued at around 48.7 billion dollars. Strongly visible household brands with a history of sports tie-ins.

LendInvest is a UK property finance company that provides buy-to-let mortgages and short-term bridging and development loans, using a digital platform and funded by institutional and retail investors. Headquartered in London; founded 2008. Funding shown is around 4.1 billion dollars, likely including debt lines. Originated billions of pounds of loans. Privately held, with a small bond listing. Known to landlords and property investors, with a limited consumer profile.

LIV Golf is a professional golf league launched in 2022 that is funded by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, with 54-hole team events, big prize money and players such as Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau. Run from the UK and US by Greg Norman as chief and later by Scott O'Neil. Funding shown is about 6.5 billion dollars. Prominent in sports media and a controversy for sportswashing concerns. High sports visibility and an active sponsorship portfolio.

Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment owns and operates the Toronto Maple Leafs (NHL), Toronto Raptors (NBA), Toronto FC (MLS) and Toronto Argonauts (CFL), and venues Scotiabank Arena and BMO Field. Earns from tickets, sponsorship, media rights and hospitality. Headquartered in Toronto. Owned by Bell and Rogers, which each hold 37.5 percent, with Larry Tanenbaum holding the remaining stake. A leading Canadian sports brand with strong fan base and existing sponsorship business.

Marriott International is the world's largest hotel company by rooms, with over 9,000 properties and 30 brands such as Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, W, Sheraton, Westin, Courtyard, JW Marriott and Marriott Bonvoy loyalty with over 200 million members. Earns franchise and management fees, with revenue near 25 billion dollars. Headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland; founded 1927. Listed on Nasdaq (MAR). Very strong consumer brands with significant sports and events partnerships.

Medline Industries is the largest privately held US maker and distributor of medical supplies, with over 335,000 products for hospitals, nursing homes, surgery centres and physician offices, and an e-commerce business. Revenue near 25 billion dollars. Headquartered in Northfield, Illinois; founded 1966 by the Mills family. Acquired by Blackstone, Carlyle and Hellman & Friedman in 2021 and listed on Nasdaq (MDLN) in a December 2025 IPO. B2B brand, little consumer awareness.

Nubank is a Latin American digital bank offering credit cards, savings, loans, insurance and investments via a mobile app, with more than 110 million customers in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. Headquartered in Sao Paulo; founded 2013 by David Velez, Cristina Junqueira and Edward Wible. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NU), with revenue near 12 billion dollars. Strong consumer brand and a purple fintech with sports marketing, such as football sponsorship in Brazil.

Octane is a US fintech offering financing for powersports vehicles, such as motorcycles, ATVs, boats and RVs, and has been moving into other consumer lending, with online approvals at dealerships. Headquartered in New York. Backed by investors including Valar Ventures. Funding shown is around 7.1 billion dollars, which includes debt facilities. B2B2C brand with limited consumer awareness.

Peranel is, according to Crunchbase, a company based in Paris that manages global water and related operations, tagged under food and beverage and water. Funding shown is about 5.9 billion in the input's currency. The input does not give products, owners, customers or scale, and the name does not match a company we recognise with confidence. Limited public information - check before outreach.

Rocket Companies is a US financial technology holding company, with Rocket Mortgage, Rocket Homes, Rocket Loans and Rocket Money, plus the acquired Redfin and Mr. Cooper. Provides online home loans, personal loans and personal finance tools to consumers. Revenue near 5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Detroit, Michigan; founded by Dan Gilbert as Quicken Loans in 1985. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RKT). Strong US consumer brand, famous for its Super Bowl advertising and naming rights to Rocket Arena in Cleveland.

Sunwoda Electric Vehicle Battery is the EV battery unit of Sunwoda, a Chinese lithium battery maker, producing cells and packs for passenger cars and commercial vehicles and for energy storage. Based in Shenzhen, Guangdong. Parent Sunwoda Electronic is listed in Shenzhen (300207); the EV unit raised funding of about 19 billion yuan. B2B supplier with limited consumer awareness.

Wayfair is a US online retailer of home furnishings, decor and housewares, with Wayfair, Joss & Main, AllModern, Birch Lane and Perigold, offering several million products and opening physical stores. Revenue near 12 billion dollars and about 20 million active customers. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts; founded 2002. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (W). Strong consumer e-commerce brand with heavy performance marketing and occasional sports sponsorships.

Bending Spoons is an Italian technology company that buys established digital products and apps, including Evernote, WeTransfer, Vimeo, AOL, Eventbrite and Meetup, and runs them using a centralised team to cut costs and raise subscription revenue. Also builds its own apps such as Remini and Splice. Headquartered in Milan; founded 2013. Raised funding at a valuation of over 11 billion dollars. Private. Corporate name is little known; its apps have large consumer user bases. Input location data is missing.

Grover is a German consumer electronics rental company offering subscriptions to phones, laptops, wearables, cameras and appliances for flexible months. Headquartered in Berlin; founded 2015. Customers are consumers and businesses in Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Spain and the US. Raised significant venture and debt funding, shown at around 2.3 billion dollars, including large debt facilities. Private. Well-known among young European consumers with strong digital marketing.

ShareChat is an Indian social media company with the ShareChat regional-language social network and the Moj short video app, serving users across Indian languages with advertising and creator tools. Headquartered in Bengaluru; founded 2015 by IIT Kanpur graduates and operates under Mohalla Tech. Backed by Twitter (earlier), Tiger Global and Temasek, valued at around 5 billion dollars in 2022. Private. Mass-market consumer brand in India.

UNISOC is a Chinese fabless chip designer making mobile processors (including 4G and 5G smartphone chips), IoT and TV chips, formerly Spreadtrum and RDA, and sells to phone makers such as Samsung, Transsion and Realme. Headquartered in Shanghai. Backed by Tsinghua Unigroup, and later by state funds and Chinese investors. Funding shown is about 2.1 billion dollars. B2B chip supplier with minimal consumer awareness.

Bitfarms is a bitcoin mining company with data centers in Canada, the US (Pennsylvania, Washington state) and Paraguay and Argentina, and it has said it will move toward high-performance computing and AI hosting. Founded 2017; originally based in Toronto, though the input shows New York. Listed on Nasdaq and the Toronto Stock Exchange (BITF). Revenue is driven by bitcoin prices. B2B-style company with little consumer awareness, known among crypto investors.

Ceconomy is the German parent of consumer electronics retailers MediaMarkt and Saturn, which run hundreds of stores in Europe, with an online and services business. Revenue near 23 billion euros. Headquartered in Dusseldorf; separated from Metro in 2017. Listed in Frankfurt (CEC). China's JD.com agreed in 2025 to acquire Ceconomy for roughly 2.2 billion euros. MediaMarkt and Saturn are well-known consumer brands across Europe with a history of football and sports sponsorship.

Hawaiian Electric Industries is the Hawaii holding company for Hawaiian Electric, the state's electric utility serving most of its population, and American Savings Bank (sold stake in 2025 plan). Earns regulated utility revenue of roughly 3.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Honolulu. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (HE). The utility faced major legal liabilities after the August 2023 Maui wildfires. Known locally in Hawaii, with a regulated service and no wider consumer reach.

International Airlines Group (IAG) is the parent of British Airways, Iberia, Vueling, Aer Lingus, Level and the loyalty scheme Avios, flying to more than 200 destinations and carrying over 100 million passengers a year. Revenue near 33 billion euros. Headquartered in London (with Madrid origins), formed 2011. Listed in London and Madrid (IAG). Strong airline brands with substantial sponsorships, such as British Airways' links to sport.

Pump.fun is a memecoin launchpad on the Solana blockchain that lets users create and trade tokens instantly without coding, earning trading fees. Launched in January 2024 by a small team and became a major crypto platform, with its own PUMP token released in 2025. Funding shown is about 1.3 billion dollars, probably from token sales. Based, per the input, in Solana Beach, California. Well known in crypto circles, controversial for speculation and legal claims.

AvidXchange provides accounts payable automation and payment software for mid-market businesses in the US, handling invoices, approvals and payments, and a network of suppliers. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina; founded 2000. Listed on Nasdaq (AVDX) in 2021 and taken private by TPG in 2025 in a deal valued at about 2.2 billion dollars. B2B brand with no consumer awareness, though it had sponsored sports and naming rights in Charlotte.

Hometap is a US fintech that offers homeowners cash in exchange for a share of their home's future value through home equity investments, instead of loans, with no monthly payments. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts; founded 2017. Raised significant funding, shown as about 1 billion dollars including capital for investment. Private. Consumer-facing brand with modest awareness among homeowners.

MoonPay is a crypto payments company that lets people buy, sell and swap digital assets with cards and bank transfers through its own app and by embedding its on-ramp in wallets and exchanges, with an NFT and stablecoin business. Headquartered in New York; founded in 2018 by Ivan Soto-Wright and Victor Faramond. Private, funded around 1 billion dollars. Consumer and B2B brand in crypto with big sports and celebrity partnerships.

MPOWER Financing provides student loans without a cosigner or collateral to international students and immigrants studying in the US and Canada, plus scholarships and immigration support. Headquartered in Washington, DC; founded 2014 by Manu Smadja and Isabelle Bronsert. Funding shown is about 940 million dollars, mostly debt capital. Private. Well known among international students, little broader awareness.

Nakamoto Holdings is a Utah-based company created by David Bailey's Nakamoto bitcoin treasury strategy through a 2025 merger with healthcare company KindlyMD (Murray, Utah), which holds a large bitcoin balance and plans to buy more. Listed on Nasdaq (NAKA). Funding shown is about 965 million dollars. Investor-focused brand, with no wider consumer recognition.

Remitly is a digital remittance company allowing migrants to send money from the US, Canada, UK, EU, Australia and other countries to over 170 receiving countries through a mobile app, with fast transfers and transparent fees. Revenue near 1.6 billion dollars. Headquartered in Seattle, Washington; founded 2011. Listed on Nasdaq (RELY) since 2021. Strong consumer brand in migrant communities and active in sports sponsorship.

Videotron is a Quebec-based telecommunications and media company, owned by Quebecor, offering mobile, internet, television and cable services, with Freedom Mobile acquired in 2023 expanding it nationally. Customers are consumers and businesses mostly in Quebec, with the new Freedom mobile brand elsewhere in Canada. Headquartered in Montreal. Parent Quebecor is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (QBR.B). Funding shown is about 1.5 billion Canadian dollars. Strong consumer brand in Quebec.

Worldline is a French payments and transactional services company, processing card payments for merchants, banks and public sector clients in Europe and beyond, with terminals, e-commerce acquiring and digital banking. Revenue near 4.6 billion euros. Headquartered in Puteaux near Paris; spun out of Atos in 2014 and listed on Euronext Paris (WLN). Working through financial pressure and restructuring in 2025. B2B brand with limited consumer awareness, though it has sponsored cycling and events.
